h1: EV Charger Installation in Broward County
intro: A home EV charger is only as safe as the electrical service behind it. The question is not which charger you buy, but whether your panel can carry a Level 2 load for hours. We check the service first and tell you plainly what it can handle.

definition.heading: What is EV charger installation
definition.body: A dedicated 240 volt circuit and unit so an electric vehicle charges safely at home. The real work is not mounting the box, it is confirming the panel, wiring, and service can carry a heavy, steady load for hours without heat or nuisance trips.

symptoms.title: A new EV and a slow trickle at the outlet
symptoms.body: A standard outlet was never meant for this. A dedicated circuit is what lets you leave each morning fully charged.

symptoms.title: The breaker trips when the car is charging
symptoms.body: The panel is telling you the load is more than the circuit was built to carry. It needs a look before it becomes a hazard.

symptoms.title: The panel is full, or the home predates electric cars
symptoms.body: Every slot is taken, or the service was sized decades ago for a home that never imagined an EV. Answer the capacity question before you commit to a charger.

symptoms.title: A warm cord or a discolored outlet
symptoms.body: Heat where there should be none, and a fire risk. Stop using it and have the circuit assessed right away.

localSections.heading: South Florida homes and the panels they were built with
localSections.body: Much of Broward's housing predates the EV, wired for the appliances of the 1960s, 70s, and 80s. Some of those panels are still sound, others are known problem brands. We check the service before we talk about the charger at all.

localSections.heading: Heat, humidity, and salt air are part of the job
localSections.body: Heat, humidity, and coastal salt air are hard on connections, and a charging circuit runs warm because it carries a heavy load for hours. We account for it with proper conductors, solid terminations, and hardware rated for the location.

guide.title: The honest guide to installing an EV charger at home in South Florida

sections.heading: Start with the service, not the charger
sections.body: People buy the car first and worry about charging second. The charger is the easy part. A Level 2 unit pulls a heavy, steady load for hours on top of the air conditioning, water heater, and range, so the service is what decides whether it is safe. Sometimes it goes right in, sometimes the service needs work first.

sections.heading: Level 1 and Level 2, in plain language
sections.body: Level 1 is the cord that comes with the car and plugs into a wall outlet. It works, but it adds only a few miles an hour. Level 2 runs on 240 volts and usually fills the car overnight, which is what makes an EV livable. It needs a dedicated circuit and enough service capacity.

sections.heading: What a proper install actually includes
sections.body: A proper install starts with conductors sized for the steady load, not the smallest wire that passes. The breaker is matched to the circuit, connections are solid, and the run is protected for its location. A charger pulls hard for hours a night for years, so it has to be built to carry that.

faqs.question: Can any home get an EV charger?
faqs.answer: Almost any home can, but not every home as it stands today. It depends on whether the service can carry the steady load. Some homes are ready right away, some need an upgrade first.

faqs.question: How do I know if my panel can handle a charger?
faqs.answer: Not from the outside. It depends on the panel's rating, how full it is, the size of the incoming service, and how much the home already draws at once. We assess all of it and give you a clear answer.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit for an EV charger?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes. Broward building departments expect a dedicated 240 volt circuit to be permitted and inspected. We pull it in our own name and meet the inspector, so you are not chasing paperwork.

faqs.question: Do you install EV chargers for commercial properties?
faqs.answer: Yes, homes and commercial properties across Broward County. Commercial installs raise the same capacity question at a larger scale, and we answer it the same way.
